title: Refactor SNAT allocator to enforce per-peering affinity and prevent cross-tenant DNS collisions
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Summary: Multiple customers on Dedicated reported intermittent cross-tenant DNS responses and brief hostname hijacks during VPC peering failovers. Investigation revealed the SNAT port allocator could reassign ephemeral port ranges without preserving peering-session affinity, combined with asymmetric encapsulation path selection. During peering handoffs the allocator reused ports tied to a recently-closed mapping which allowed resolver replies to be accepted and associated with the wrong tenant until cache/TCP state aged out. This produced brief spikes of DNS resolution anomalies and in two cases caused cross-tenant service misattribution.
observed_behavior:
- DNS A/AAAA and CNAME replies occasionally resolved to the wrong tenant following a peering swap or manual failover.
- Failures lasted between 20s and 3m depending on resolver cache and conntrack state.
- Customers saw increased 5xx errors for service discovery calls and inconsistent metrics attribution during the window.
root_cause:
- The SNAT allocator used a global pool with a best-effort reuse policy. When a peering session moved, ephemeral port ranges were returned to the global pool immediately.
- There was no binding between peering session identity (peer VNI + tenant ID) and ephemeral port subranges.
- An existing asymmetric encapsulation path in the fabric caused some return traffic to hit different NAT engines which accepted replies for recently-freed ports.
- Conntrack entries persisted long enough that reply packets were accepted and attributed incorrectly before being flushed.
mitigation_and_fix:
Short-term mitigation (in incident):
- Implemented eager conntrack teardown on peering state change for affected tenant aggregates.
- Added a temporary guard in the allocator to quiesce returned port ranges for 5 minutes before reallocation.
- Notified impacted customers, applied per-tenant resolver affinity where possible, and opened support tickets.

Permanent fix (this ticket):
1) Refactor SNAT allocator to maintain per-peering-session subpool reservation. Port subranges are now pinned to (tenant-id, peering-session-id) for a configurable grace interval post-teardown.
2) Introduced allocator deterministic hashing so parallel allocator instances do not conflict during handoffs.
3) Added e2e tests that simulate peering failover and asymmetric return paths with packet replay to validate non-reuse guarantees.
4) Deployed a gradual rollout: canary on 3 clusters -> staggered rollout across Dedicated regions -> full.
5) Added observability: new Datadog metrics allocator.port_reuse_skips, allocator.quiesce_count and a dashboard for peering-affinity-misses.

Code artifacts: PR #https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/4217, RFC doc https://docs.internal.redwood.ai/networking/snat-affinity-rfc, and unit + e2e test suites under infrastructure/tests/snat.
deployment_plan:
Canary: 2026-03-02 on dedicated-prod-canary-3 (low-traffic tenant pool).
Validation window: 2 hours of steady traffic + synthetic DNS load tests.
Stagger: roll canary -> 15% region -> 50% region -> 100% region in 24h -> monitor 72h before releasing to all Dedicated clusters.
Rollback: feature flag to disable per-peering pinning and revert allocator to previous behavior; immediate conntrack flush across affected nodes.
Post-deploy checks: allocator.port_reuse_skips == 0 for newly pinned ranges, reduced DNS anomaly alerts, no increase in SNAT exhaustion metrics.
verification:
- Ran replay harness simulating peering stomps 10k times; observed zero cross-tenant DNS reply acceptance.
- Canary: no additional customer escalations in the 72h window, latency stable, and estimated token egress costs unchanged.
- Synthetic load: 99.9th percentile DNS latency unchanged, 50th improved marginally due to reduced retry storms.
- Added an automated integration test in CI that reproduces the previous failure mode and asserts zero leakage.
postmortem_and_followups:
Postmortem doc: https://incidents.redwood.ai/2026/02/snat-peering-dns-leak-postmortem.
Follow-ups:
- ENG-130212: Expand allocator sharding to reduce headroom, lower risk of port exhaustion.
- ENG-131900: Harden dataplane encapsulation path selection to avoid asymmetric return paths during peering transitions.
- PM task: communicate long-term SLA changes for Dedicated tenants and update onboarding docs.
- Design/UX: add clearer customer-facing notes in Console about failover behavior and mitigation knobs.
customer_communication:
- Initial incident notification to affected customers sent 2026-02-24 with ETA for fix.
- Detailed postmortem shared 2026-03-11 with mitigation, timeline, and compensatory credits offer where appropriate.
- Internal support playbook updated with triage steps and a script to run conntrack flushes safely on nodes.
